Business case: assessing candidates before the interview
November 2026 · Engineering roles
The problem
You plan 100 engineering hires in the next 12 months. Your engineers will spend about 2,600 hours interviewing, $312,000 of their time. 17 of every 18 candidates you interview do not get the job.
What changes
Every candidate completes a work simulation in Codility Screen before the interview, in a real coding environment where they can use Claude Code and Codex. AI assistance is enabled or disabled per task, and AI usage is included with no API keys to set up. Your engineers interview the candidates whose work holds up.
If that removes 7 candidates per hire from your interview list, your team gets back about 1,010 hours and $121,300 of interviewer time a year.
What engineering leaders and finance will ask
Will our engineers trust the results?
Every work simulation is built from a library of 1,300+ tasks validated by the Codility assessment science team.
How is AI use handled?
AI assistance is enabled or disabled per task, and every interaction is saved as reviewable AI activity.
How is integrity handled?
Layered integrity signals, including ID verification, behavioral monitoring and risk scoring, with the evidence kept for human review.
How do candidates feel about it?
9 in 10 candidates say the assessment content is fair, from 48,000+ candidate responses, October 2025 to April 2026.
You plan 100 hires in sales in the next 12 months. Your hiring managers will spend about 1,300 hours interviewing, $97,500 of their time. 10 of every 11 candidates you interview do not get the job.
Every candidate completes a Codility AI skills assessment before the interview: a real deliverable for the role, produced with an AI assistant and scored against a documented method. Your hiring managers interview the candidates whose work holds up.
If that removes 3 candidates per hire from your interview list, your team gets back about 350 hours and $26,600 of interviewer time a year.
What talent, legal and your AI ethics committee will ask
What exactly is measured?
Getting real work done with AI: giving context, directing the assistant, judging its output and delivering the result.
Who scores it?
The deliverable is scored deterministically against a documented method, and the full AI transcript stays reviewable.
Is this a new system?
It runs on the same platform, scoring, reporting, integrations and compliance posture as Codility’s engineering assessments, refined over almost two decades.
Does it fit our process?
Results flow into your applicant tracking system through Codility’s integrations.
Run Codility on one open role this quarter. Compare interviewer hours and the share of interviewed candidates who get an offer against the figures above.
Method and sources
Figures combine your inputs with public benchmarks from Gem’s 2026 and 2025 Recruiting Benchmarks, Ashby Talent Trends and Metaview. Time back uses your average interviewer time per candidate. Hours are rounded to the nearest 10 and dollars to the nearest $100.

How the numbers work
Every figure in the calculator is arithmetic on your inputs, and every default comes from a published benchmark. Here is the whole method.
The arithmetic
Interview time a year = hires × interviewer hours per hire.
Interviewer cost = interview time × the hourly cost of your interviewers.
Full working years = interview time ÷ 2,080 hours.
Average interviewer hours per candidate = interviewer hours per hire ÷ candidates interviewed per hire.
Time back = hires × candidates you would no longer interview × average interviewer hours per candidate. Finalists take the most time, so set your scenario with your own drop-off in mind.
Hours are rounded to the nearest 10 and dollars to the nearest $100.
